sso.error.sso_required: Your organization requires single sign-on. Choose “Continue with single sign-on” and sign in at your organization’s identity provider first.
sso.error.sso_expired: This sign-in has expired or was started in another window. Start it again from this window.
sso.error.sso_failed: Single sign-on did not work. Try again; if it keeps failing, ask your administrator.
sso.error.sso_not_configured: Your organization has not set up single sign-on (or turned it off). Sign in with your master password and Secret Key.
sso.error.sso_public_url_missing: The server does not know its public address (PASSBOX_PUBLIC_URL), so the identity provider cannot send you back. Ask your administrator to set it.
sso.error.sso_idp_denied: The identity provider did not complete the sign-in (cancelled or not allowed). Try again, or ask your administrator whether Passbox is assigned to you.
sso.error.sso_token_rejected: The identity provider rejected the request. The client ID, client secret or redirect URI is probably wrong; ask your administrator to check the settings.
sso.error.sso_invalid_token: The identity provider’s answer could not be verified (signature, issuer, audience or expiry). Try again; if it persists, the configuration needs checking.
sso.error.sso_unreachable: The identity provider could not be reached. Check the issuer URL and that the server can reach it.
sso.error.sso_insecure_url: The identity provider must use https://. Enter the issuer URL with https.
sso.error.sso_http_error: The identity provider answered with an error. Check the issuer URL.
sso.error.sso_invalid_response: The identity provider sent an answer Passbox cannot read. Check that the issuer URL points to an OpenID Connect provider.
sso.error.sso_issuer_mismatch: The discovery document names a different issuer. Copy the issuer URL exactly as your provider shows it.
sso.error.sso_unsupported_provider: The provider does not offer what Passbox needs: the authorization code flow with S256 PKCE and RS256, PS256 or ES256 signatures.
sso.error.sso_no_email: The identity provider did not send an email address. Add the email scope or set the email claim in the advanced settings.
sso.error.sso_email_unverified: The identity provider says this email address is not verified. Verify it there, or ask your administrator.
sso.error.sso_domain_not_allowed: This email domain may not sign in through this organization. Ask your administrator to add it.
sso.error.sso_domain_taken: {domain} already signs in through another organization on this server. Each email domain belongs to one organization.
sso.error.sso_not_member: You are not a member of this organization in Passbox yet. Accept the invitation in the mail you received, or ask an administrator to invite you.
sso.error.sso_suspended: Your membership in this organization is suspended. Ask an administrator.
sso.error.sso_no_account: There is no Passbox account for this email yet. Create an account first.
sso.error.sso_proof_invalid: The single sign-on has expired or was already used. Sign in with single sign-on again.
sso.error.sso_team_only: Single sign-on is available for team organizations.
sso.error.sso_device_unlock_not_allowed: Your organization does not allow unlocking with single sign-on. Use your master password.
sso.error.sso_device_not_trusted: This device is no longer trusted. Unlock with your master password or ask a trusted device to approve this one.
sso.error.sso_request_expired: The approval request has expired. Sign in with single sign-on again to ask once more.
sso.error.account_disabled: This account has been disabled by an administrator.
sso.signIn.required: Your organization requires signing in through {name}.
sso.signIn.notFound: No organization uses single sign-on for this email domain. Sign in with your master password and Secret Key.
sso.signIn.dialogText: Enter your work email. Passbox sends you to your organization’s identity provider.
sso.unlock.trusted: This device is trusted. {name} confirms it is you, then Passbox unlocks without the master password.
sso.unlock.newDevice: {name} can confirm it is you; the master password follows.
sso.callback.passwordUnlock: Enter your master password to decrypt your data. Single sign-on proves who you are, but only you can decrypt.
sso.callback.passwordNewDevice: On a new device, Passbox also needs your Secret Key (it is in your Emergency Kit). Single sign-on proves who you are, but only you can decrypt.
sso.callback.proofUsed: This sign-in was used. To try again, sign in with single sign-on once more.
sso.callback.noPasswordText: A device where you are signed in (and that is trusted for single sign-on) can approve this one. Afterwards this device unlocks with single sign-on.
sso.noAccount.title: No Passbox account yet
sso.noAccount.text: Your organization confirmed {email}, but there is no Passbox account for it on this server. Create one with this email; then sign in with single sign-on.
sso.approval.waitText: Open Passbox on a device where you are signed in, go to Settings → Trusted devices and choose “Review” for this request.
sso.approval.where: Compare this code with the one the other device shows. Approve only if they match.
sso.approval.denied: The request was declined. Close this screen and sign in with your master password.
sso.devices.title: Trusted devices
sso.devices.description: Trusted devices unlock with your organization’s single sign-on instead of the master password.
sso.devices.thisBrowserText: A key for this browser opens your account key after a single sign-on. It is stored in this browser profile and cannot be read out by scripts, but anyone who controls this computer and your identity provider account could unlock. Trust only your own devices.
sso.devices.trusted: This browser now unlocks with single sign-on.
sso.devices.removeText: The device then needs the master password (and the Secret Key) again. It keeps nothing that opens your account key.
sso.devices.removeFailed: The device could not be removed.
sso.devices.reviewText: The new device shows a code. Approve only if it matches the code below and you started the request yourself.
sso.devices.codeMatches: The code on the new device matches
sso.devices.reviewWarning: Approving gives that device access to your whole account after a single sign-on. If you did not start this, decline and tell your administrator.
sso.devices.approved: The device is approved and trusted.
sso.settings.title: Single sign-on
sso.settings.description: Sign-in through your identity provider and provisioning for {org}.
sso.settings.entryText: OpenID Connect sign-in, SSO unlock on trusted devices and SCIM provisioning.
sso.settings.teamOnly: Single sign-on is available for team organizations.
sso.settings.adminsOnly: Only owners and admins of this organization can change single sign-on.
sso.settings.oidcDescription: Members confirm who they are at your identity provider. Decrypting still needs their master password and Secret Key, unless the device is trusted.
sso.settings.displayNameHint: Members see it when they sign in.
sso.settings.issuerHint: Passbox reads /.well-known/openid-configuration below this URL. Copy it exactly from your provider.
sso.settings.secretStored: Stored – leave empty to keep it
sso.settings.clientSecretHint: Stored encrypted on the server and never shown again.
sso.settings.redirectUriHint: Register exactly this URI at your identity provider.
sso.settings.redirectUriMissing: The server needs PASSBOX_PUBLIC_URL to know its redirect URI.
sso.settings.domainsHint: One per line. People with these domains are offered this sign-in. A domain belongs to one organization on this server.
sso.settings.reauthHours: Sign in with SSO again after (hours)
sso.settings.reauthHoursHint: With “Require single sign-on”, a device is remembered this long.
sso.settings.requireVerifiedText: Only accept addresses the provider marks as verified (email_verified). Turn it off for Microsoft Entra ID, which does not send this claim.
sso.settings.enabledText: Members with the domains above can sign in through the identity provider.
sso.settings.requiredText: Members must sign in through the identity provider. Owners and admins can always use the master password, so a broken provider cannot lock everyone out.
sso.settings.deviceUnlockText: Members can trust their devices and then unlock without the master password. The account key is then protected by the device key and the identity provider instead of the master password.
sso.settings.checkFailed: The connection could not be checked.
sso.settings.removeText: Members then sign in with the master password and Secret Key only. Links to provider accounts, the email domains and pending approvals are deleted. Trusted devices fall back to the master password.
sso.settings.removeFailed: Single sign-on could not be removed.
sso.check.ok: The provider is reachable and publishes {keys, plural, one {# signing key} other {# signing keys}}.
sso.test.saveFirst: Save the settings to test a sign-in.
sso.test.failed: The test sign-in did not work.
sso.test.popupBlocked: The browser blocked the sign-in window. Allow pop-ups for this site and try again.
sso.test.timeout: The test sign-in was not finished within 10 minutes.
sso.test.popupClose: You can close this window; the result is shown in Passbox.
sso.test.subject: Subject (sub)
sso.test.name: Name
scim.title: Provisioning (SCIM)
scim.description: Your directory creates, updates and deactivates members. Deactivating someone ends all their sessions right away.
scim.baseUrlHint: Enter it as the tenant or base URL in your identity provider, together with a token.
scim.tokens.title: Tokens
scim.tokens.none: No tokens yet. Create one for your identity provider.
scim.tokens.name: Name
scim.tokens.daysHint: 1 to 730 days. Passbox marks tokens that expire within 14 days.
scim.tokens.revokeText: The identity provider can no longer provision with it. Members stay as they are.
scim.tokens.revokeFailed: The token could not be revoked.
scim.created.title: Copy the token now
scim.created.text: It is shown only once. Paste it into your identity provider as the bearer token (secret token).
scim.created.label: SCIM token
scim.users.title: Provisioned people
scim.users.confirmFailed: The member could not be confirmed.
scim.users.pendingNote: {count, plural, one {# person joined and waits} other {# people joined and wait}} for confirmation. Confirming checks their key and seals the organization key for them; only an admin’s unlocked Passbox can do that, the server cannot.
scim.groups.title: Directory groups
scim.groups.hint: Groups from your directory with their members. Add people to Passbox groups yourself: that needs sealed keys from an admin.
